subject: [MAP] Eval map finalization — API keys, org setup, safelist, VPC peering
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Moore <alyssa.moore@healthsync.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft & environment gating (API keys, org setup, safelist, VPC peering)

Alyssa — thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a short mutual action plan (MAP_v1.3) that sequences the POC environment steps so your infra and SRE teams can plan work in parallel with our onboarding. High-level asks inside the MAP:

- Org setup: create a HealthSync org in our console and add two seats for Env SRE (devops@healthsync.com) and Platform PM.
- API keys: one short-lived evaluation key for integration (30d) + one workload key scoped to the test tenant.
- Safelist (IP allowlist): add the three HealthSync egress ranges in attachment (safelist_template.csv) and confirm CIDR notation.
- VPC peering: optional but recommended for throughput — we'll provide the peering spec and BGP hints.

Can you confirm whether your security team wants: (a) temporary eval keys only, (b) keys plus a signed MOU for limited retention, or (c) a private deployment checklist (if you need a VPC/private package)? Also flag any mandatory audit artifacts (SOC2 evidence, IP ranges for egress).

Proposed timeline (tentative): MAP sign-off by 10/16, infra prep 10/17–10/20, early integration window 10/21–10/27, acceptance test week 10/28–11/03. We can compress if you want a parallel run.

I'll loop in Grace (engineering owner) and Jordan (customer success) to coordinate the technical handoffs.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: HealthSync_MAP_v1.3.pdf, safelist_template.csv
From: Alyssa Moore <alyssa.moore@healthsync.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@healthsync.com, PS Team <ps-team@healthsync.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & environment gating (API keys, org setup, safelist, VPC peering)

Priyom — thanks for the clear MAP. Quick answers from the security/infra side:

- We prefer option (b): temp eval keys plus a signed MOU that limits retention to 45 days for this trial. We can sign and return the MOU once you send the standard template.
- Safelist: devops attached our public egress ranges; I copied devops@ to confirm the CIDRs.
- VPC peering: our SRE prefers to start with IP safelist only for the initial evaluation. We may request peering during the acceptance week depending on throughput.

One ask: can you provide a non-prod tenant with separate org-level telemetry so we can validate cost and token consumption per-route? Also need an API key with sample rate limits (we'll run a synthetic load to calibrate).

We have internal blackout on 10/19–10/20 (security audit), so the earliest sign-off we can realistically do is 10/21.

I'll have devops send the exact CIDR list in a follow-up.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Moore
Director, Platform Operations | HealthSync
alyssa.moore@healthsync.com
From: DevOps Team <devops@healthsync.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & environment gating (API keys, org setup, safelist, VPC peering)

Hi team — attaching the CIDR block list for our egress and the service account names we prefer to use for the initial integration. Please confirm the exact hostnames you'll expect in the safelist and whether we should reserve a /29 for testing peering.

CIDRs: 34.82.112.0/22, 52.12.128.0/20, 18.204.32.0/21
Service accounts: healthsync-sre-testing@healthsync.com, healthsync-poc@healthsync.com

Also: a couple of operational clarifications we need before we generate the skeleton resources:
- Would the eval API key be project-scoped or org-scoped? We prefer org-scoped keys that can later be rotated via your console.
- For safelist verification, do you only require source IPs or also specific egress ports (443 outbound only)?

Thanks —
HealthSync DevOps
(Attached: safelist_template_filled.csv)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Moore <alyssa.moore@healthsync.com>, devops@healthsync.com
Cc: Priyom Das <priom.das@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft & environment gating (API keys, org setup, safelist, VPC peering)

Alyssa / DevOps — thanks for the CIDRs and the service account names. Quick technical confirmations and next steps from our side:

- Org: we've provisioned healthsync-eval-01 in our console and invited healthsync-sre-testing@healthsync.com and healthsync-poc@healthsync.com as organization_sre. You should see invites in your inbox (please accept to complete onboarding).
- API keys: we'll create an org-scoped eval key with a 30-day TTL and the following scopes: generate:text, embeddings:read, admin:logs (read-only). Once we receive the signed MOU we'll extend TTL to 45 days and re-issue.
- Safelist: Redwood accepts source IP ranges on port 443 outbound. We will publish the hostnames you need to allow by EOD (two hostnames: runtime.prod1.redwood-inference.com and runtime.prod2.redwood-inference.com).
- VPC peering: leaving as opt-in. If you request peering later we'll send the peering spec and schedule a short RFC call to walk BGP/route exchange.

Acceptance criteria (for the MAP closing):
1) HealthSync accepts the org invite and confirms two SRE seats.
2) DevOps confirms safelist entries are active and can reach runtime.prod1.redwood-inference.com:443 from your test subnet.
3) Redwood delivers an example workload run (synthetic scripts) and a usage report showing token counts and average p99 latency under the test load.
4) Mutual sign-off on MOU and log retention window.

Given your audit blackout, we will target the integration window 10/21–10/27 and acceptance checklist on 10/28. Jordan will run a short playbook during acceptance week and collect the telemetry snapshots.

If that works I will attach the MOU template and the short test harness tomorrow.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
